title: Repeat-Return Surcharge — Benefit Overpayment Accounts Desk Guidance
content:
A repeat-return surcharge is added to the face charge of the returned-payment fee on Benefit Overpayment Accounts for the other return entries booked on the overpayment within the return look-back period, each return entry counting as one returned item.

| Other return entries on the overpayment within the return look-back period | Surcharge added |
|---|---|
| Two or more | USD 15.00, the multiple-return surcharge |
| Exactly one | USD 10.00, the single-return surcharge |
| None | Nothing |

The return being charged is never counted as another return. A return entry falls inside a look-back of a given number of months when the whole months from its booking date to the handling date are fewer than that number.

## How the other returns are counted

The other returns are the return entries booked on the overpayment that fall inside the return look-back period, less the return being charged.

| Return entries inside the look-back, the charged one included | Other returns | Surcharge |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | Nothing |
| 2 | 1 | USD 10.00 |
| 3 | 2 | USD 15.00 |
| 5 | 4 | USD 15.00 |

## Questions the rule answers

**Does a return booked on another overpayment count?** No. Only return entries booked on the same overpayment count.

**A look-back of 4 months applies, the handling date is 20 June, and an earlier return was booked on 10 February (hypothetical dates). Does it count?** From 10 February to 20 June is four whole months, which is not fewer than 4, so it falls outside the look-back and does not count. A return booked on 25 February, three whole months before 20 June, falls inside.
